_about: Optional written view per upcoming game, keyed by ESPN game id: {"text": "...", "sources": [urls], "written_at": ISO}. Shown on the game page as 'Analyst view' (locker-room news, trade rumours, a player facing his former team...). Never mixed into the numbers.

401910007.text: Ty Jerome, Memphis' leading scorer at about 25 a game, misses a third straight game with a hip impingement, and he would have been facing Cleveland, his former team. Isaiah Stewart (illness) is also out and Memphis play the first night of a back-to-back, though they are 7-0 on the road. Cleveland are still without Evan Mobley (toe) for at least another week. With Jerome out, the angle leans slightly towards Cleveland at home.

401910008.text: Houston had a four-game winning streak snapped in Miami and Amen Thompson is questionable with a sore knee, with Clint Capela out. Indiana are still without Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring), Andrew Nembhard is questionable, and the front office is testing the trade market for upgrades. The angle leans towards Houston.

401910009.text: An emotional night: Giannis Antetokounmpo faces Milwaukee for the first time after 13 seasons ('emotions are for movies'), and Miami will play a tribute video for Tyler Herro, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kel'el Ware and Kasparas Jakucionis, now Bucks. It is also the first Adebayo-Herro meeting since their July confrontation over a leaked message; Adebayo is probable after hip tightness. Milwaukee are 1-13 on a 10-game skid with 'no one really happy', so the angle leans clearly towards Miami, with Herro's motivation the wild card.

401910010.text: Philadelphia lose Jaylen Brown to a left hamstring strain after he scored 31 in each of his last two games; he will be re-evaluated before Saturday. LeBron James and Joel Embiid are expected to play, while Orlando are still without Paolo Banchero and Jonathan Isaac but have won four straight. With Brown out, the angle leans slightly towards Orlando.

401910011.text: Nic Claxton returns to Brooklyn for the first time since the June three-team trade that sent him to Chicago. Both teams are 3-10, and the Nets are reportedly willing to listen on almost anyone, with Michael Porter Jr. expected to be shopped. Chicago are without rookie Caleb Wilson; the angle is close to neutral with a slight lean to Brooklyn at home.

401910012.text: Toronto lost a fifth straight on Tuesday, their 15th in a row against New York, with Kawhi Leonard sitting for knee management, and now play the second night of a back-to-back. Washington have lost eight straight, Brian Keefe cut short his press conference after the 28-point loss in Houston, and his seat is being described as warm. Two frustrated teams; the angle leans mildly towards Toronto at home.

401910013.text: Detroit arrive on a high after ending San Antonio's 12-game winning streak on Tuesday, but on the second night of a back-to-back and without Jalen Duren, Duncan Robinson and Isaiah Joe. New Orleans are without trade-requester Dejounte Murray (ankle) and Trey Murphy III, and are 1-8 with Murray in the lineup. The angle leans towards Detroit, with fatigue the main counterweight.

401910014.text: Lu Dort and Aaron Wiggins return to Oklahoma City for the first time since being traded for second-round picks; Dort called it 'a lot of memories', while Wiggins says 'this is who I represent now'. Atlanta are banged up, with CJ McCollum out about four weeks (calf). The angle leans towards the Thunder, with some extra fire from the returning Hawks.

401910016.text: Golden State are 1-3 without Stephen Curry (oblique), have lost three straight, and Draymond Green and Al Horford are questionable, with ESPN suggesting they may sit one end of the Dallas-Memphis back-to-back. Kristaps Porzingis remains away from the team. Dallas have lost three straight, conceding 127-plus each time, and Dusty May says they are 'looking each other in the mirror'. The angle leans towards Dallas.

401910015.text: Boston bring a clean injury report after being out-muscled 54-32 in the paint at Orlando, while Denver are 2-4 at home and were booed after Monday's loss to Phoenix. A frustrated Nuggets side should want a response, but nothing off the stat sheet stands out beyond that. The angle is close to neutral with a slight lean to Boston.

401910017.text: Utah snapped a 12-game losing streak on Tuesday as Brice Sensabaugh scored 40 off the bench against the Clippers, so they arrive with some life despite the back-to-back. JJ Redick expects Walker Kessler to play against the team that traded him, and Austin Reaves will try to return from his heel bruise; the Lakers are also on a back-to-back. The angle leans towards the Lakers.

401910018.text: Sacramento are 1-12 and 0-8 at home, one loss from tying the worst start in franchise history, with Doug Christie saying 'the seat is hot, always' and Domantas Sabonis reported to want out. Phoenix won in Denver on Monday for their first road win. The angle leans towards Phoenix, against a home side under heavy pressure.

401910019.text: Both teams are on the second night of a back-to-back. Golden State are without Stephen Curry, have lost three straight, and Draymond Green or Al Horford may sit one of the two nights. Memphis have won seven straight on the road, but Ty Jerome's hip remains a question. The angle leans towards Memphis at home.

401910020.text: Damian Lillard faces Milwaukee, where he tore his Achilles, while Deni Avdija (sore left foot) is out. The Bucks are 1-13 on a 10-game skid, Taylor Jenkins has used 150 different lineups, and Tyler Herro's second-half benching against Atlanta has added friction; they also play the night after Giannis's return game in Miami. The angle leans clearly towards Portland.

401910021.text: Karl-Anthony Towns returns to Minnesota after two straight wins in Toronto, saying the Knicks 'played like the Knicks again'. Minnesota are without Anthony Edwards (knee surgery), Jonathan Kuminga (shoulder) and Donte DiVincenzo (Achilles), though they edged Portland on Tuesday. The angle leans slightly towards New York despite the road trip.

401910022.text: San Antonio's 12-game winning streak ended against Detroit, and Dylan Harper was helped off holding his groin, with no diagnosis yet. The Clippers were hammered by 25 in Utah, Bradley Beal misses the whole trip, but Brandon Ingram may make his season debut here. The angle still leans clearly towards the Spurs, with Harper's status worth watching.
